criteria.name: Problem passes the swap-test
criteria.rationale: "Clinics are bad at scheduling, and it's the single biggest operational drag in outpatient care — every clinic is fighting its calendar and losing revenue to it" is a category claim any competing scheduling vendor could publish word for word. Naming "the clinic as a business, not the office manager" picks a buyer type but records no pain specific to this customer.

criteria.name: Appetite is a fixed tier
criteria.rationale: "small (≤2 weeks)" pairs the tier word with an explicit calendar bound, which is the literal failure mode the criterion names — a calendar estimate wearing a tier's name. Borderline, since the tier itself is stated, but a fixed-tier appetite is the budget, not an upper bound on elapsed time.

criteria.name: Solution sketch under-specified and within cap
criteria.rationale: About 95 words, no diagrams, no acceptance criteria and no exhaustive edge cases; it stays at mechanism level ("Cancellation comes in, text goes out, slot gets filled, no phone calls"), well inside the ~150-word cap.

criteria.name: Every assumption passes the falsifiability checklist
criteria.rationale: The single assumption is quantified ("claimed by someone within the hour at least half the time"), thresholded and pre-committed ("Fewer than half of offers claimed inside the hour"), not can't-fail (the measured share can land either side of half), and carries a cheap test plus a by-when (counting claims across "~60 manual waitlist offers" already in Riverbend's message log, by "Thursday 20 Aug 2026").
